claims.support: Title and theme of arable land share comparison

claims.text: A global comparison of arable land share, from the high-density fields of Bangladesh to the vast interiors of Canada and Australia.
Bangladesh has 61% arable land. In the USA, it is 17%.
Bangladesh is the world's highest. This includes land under temporary crops, gardens, and temporary fallow, but excludes abandoned shifting cultivation.
claims.support: Bangladesh rank 1; definition mentions temporary crops, gardens, temporary fallow, and excludes abandoned shifting cultivation

claims.text: Canada and Australia have just 4%. Huge countries, but very little is ready for the plow.
India has 52%. That is 3.1 times the share in the USA.
China has 12% and Japan has 11%. Both sit just above the global median of 10%.
Nigeria has 41%. A high share for a large nation, including fields left fallow.
The leaders? Bangladesh 61%, Denmark 59%, and The Gambia 58%.
claims.support: Bangladesh rank 1 (61%), Denmark rank 2 (59%), The Gambia rank 3 (58%)
